issues.title: Handler logic mixed in schema file
issues.description: The rule requires that schema and handler logic are separated into different files. However, the schema file `booking.output.ts` now contains a handler method `cleanEmailForDisplay()` that performs email validation and transformation logic, mixing schema definition with handler logic in the same file.
issues.rule_name: Schema and Handler Files Must Be Separated with Type-Safe Patterns

issues.title: Lost `this` context in displayGuests mapping causes runtime error
issues.description: In the `getOutputBooking` method at line 171, the code passes `this.getDisplayEmail` directly to the `map` function without binding the `this` context. This causes a runtime error because when `getDisplayEmail` is invoked inside the `map` callback, `this` will be `undefined`, resulting in "Cannot read property 'replace' of undefined" or similar errors. The arrow function `(guest: string) => this.getDisplayEmail(guest)` was removed, which was necessary to preserve the `this` binding. This will break all bookings that have guests.

issues.title: Recurring seated bookings returned in wrong order
issues.description: In the `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` method at line 424, the sort operation that orders bookings chronologically by start time has been removed. The original code sorted bookings with `.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.start).getTime() - new Date(b.start).getTime())` to ensure they are returned in chronological order. Without this sorting, recurring bookings will be returned in an arbitrary order (based on how they were stored in the database or map), which breaks the expected API contract and will confuse clients expecting chronological ordering of recurring events.

issues.title: Unnecessary regex processing on literal "unknown" string
issues.description: In the `getHost` method at line 219, when the user is null/unknown, the code now calls `this.getDisplayEmail("unknown")` instead of directly setting `displayEmail: "unknown"`. This causes unnecessary regex processing on the literal string "unknown" which has no CUID suffix to remove. While this doesn't break functionality, it adds unnecessary computational overhead and is semantically incorrect - the getDisplayEmail method is designed to strip CUID suffixes from actual email addresses, not process placeholder strings. This represents a performance issue and code smell that violates the principle of only processing data when necessary.

issues.title: Service file uses disallowed '.service.ts' suffix / naming convention violation
issues.description: Rule 1 disallows dot-suffix service filenames like '.service.ts' and requires service files to be named '<Entity>Service.ts' with matching PascalCase. This PR modifies a service located at 'services/output.service.ts', which violates the naming convention.
issues.rule_name: Rule 1: Repository and Service Classes Must Follow Naming Conventions

issues.title: Line(s) exceed the 110 character line width requirement
issues.description: The added assignment line is longer than the 110 character limit required by the Biome formatting rules for TS/JS files.
issues.rule_name: Rule 3: Use Biome for Code Formatting with Standardized Configuration

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25593 - fix(api): return original email without OAuth suffix in bookings

structured_output.summary:
The PR adds a `displayEmail` field next to every email in the API v2 (2024-08-13) booking responses (hosts, attendees, reassignedTo, bookingFieldsResponses, and displayGuests). The value is the original email with the `+{cuid}` OAuth-client suffix removed, so existing `email` fields stay unchanged for backward compatibility. The change is implemented as a private `getDisplayEmail` regex helper in `OutputBookingsService_2024_08_13`, with matching output DTO fields, OpenAPI doc edits, and e2e test updates.

The core idea is sound and the new managed-user e2e tests check exact values. However, the regex is unanchored, so it can corrupt addresses whose plus-tag is longer than 25 characters. The PR also silently drops the start-time sort from `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings`, which is unrelated to the feature and changes response ordering. Several test assertions compare `displayEmail` to itself, so they pass even when the field is missing.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Two defects should be fixed before merge: the unanchored regex can produce wrong email addresses (verified: `bob+cmidditrv0000mza4q93hbcau1@example.com` becomes `bob1@example.com`), and the removed sort is an unannounced behavior regression. The self-referential test assertions and the unused helper are worth fixing but are not blockers.

architecture.overview:
Booking responses for API v2 (2024-08-13) are assembled in `OutputBookingsService_2024_08_13` (`apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`). It maps database bookings, attendees, hosts, and reassignment targets into plain objects, then runs them through `plainToClass` with `excludeAll` into the DTOs in `packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/outputs/booking.output.ts`. Managed users carry an OAuth-client suffix on their email (`bob+{cuid}@example.com`) to keep them distinct across OAuth clients.

The PR adds a single pure helper, `getDisplayEmail`, that strips that suffix, and calls it at each place an email is emitted. Each call site gets a sibling `displayEmail` field, while the raw `email` field is left as-is. The helper is not applied to seated-attendee `bookingFieldsResponses`, which keep their existing privacy deletion of `email`.
steps: Entry point: booking endpoints call the output service, which maps the Prisma booking (with attendees, user, and bookingFieldsResponses) into response objects.

The new `getDisplayEmail` helper (output.service.ts ~L96) applies `/\+[a-zA-Z0-9]{25}/` once per email. It is used for attendees, `getHost`, `bookingFieldsResponses.email`, `bookingFieldsResponses.guests` (to produce `displayGuests`), and the reassignment output.

Each mapped object is then passed through `plainToClass` into DTOs. `displayEmail` is added to `BookingAttendee`, `BookingHost`, and `ReassignedToDto` in booking.output.ts, so the field is exposed (`@Expose`) and documented.

Side changes: the OpenAPI spec (`docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json`) gets hand-edited `displayEmail` schemas, and `.github/oasdiff-err-ignore.txt` suppresses the resulting oneOf diffs. Unrelated to the feature, `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` also loses its sort (output.service.ts ~L424).
Tests: e2e specs across bookings, org, and team modules add `displayEmail` expectations. The managed-user spec asserts the exact stripped values, which is the strongest coverage in the PR.

findings.title: Unanchored regex corrupts plus-tagged emails longer than 25 characters
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`, the private `getDisplayEmail` helper (around lines 96-98) uses `/\+[a-zA-Z0-9]{25}/`, which is not anchored. For an address like `bob+<26+ alnum chars>@example.com` it leaves part of the tag behind (e.g. `bob1@example.com`). Change the regex so it only matches a 25-character tag immediately before the `@` (a lookahead `(?=@)` is enough). Keep it a single `replace` call. Add a unit test in the output service spec covering a long plus-tag (should be unchanged) and the real CUID case (should be stripped). Check the same pattern in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarAuth.ts` before deciding whether to change it there too.

findings.title: Start-time sort silently removed from recurring seated bookings
findings.body:
In `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings`, the PR changes `return transformed.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.start).getTime() - new Date(b.start).getTime());` to `return transformed;`. That is unrelated to the displayEmail change and is not mentioned in the PR description. The caller gets bookings in the order of `bookingsIds`, not sorted by start, so any client that relies on chronological order of seated recurring bookings gets a silent change.

If the intent was to simplify, that belongs in a separate PR. Otherwise the sort should be restored as it was.

::diff{file="apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts" lines="410-424"}

(The sort in `getOutputCreateRecurringSeatedBookings` is still present, so the two methods are now inconsistent.)
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`, `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` (around line 424) was changed from returning a start-time-sorted array to `return transformed;`. This sort removal is unrelated to the displayEmail feature. Restore `return transformed.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.start).getTime() - new Date(b.start).getTime());`, matching `getOutputCreateRecurringSeatedBookings`. Leave the whitespace-only edits in the same method alone or move them to their own commit.

findings.title: Seated attendee displayEmail assertions compare the field to itself
findings.body:
In several seated and team e2e tests the expected value is read from the response that is being checked, for example `displayEmail: createdSeatedBooking.attendees[0].displayEmail` or `displayEmail: phoneBasedBooking.attendees[0].displayEmail`. The expected value is therefore whatever the code produced, so the assertion checks nothing about correctness.

This is worse than a weak assertion. Jest's `toEqual` ignores `undefined` properties, so if `displayEmail` is missing from the response, both sides are `undefined` and the test still passes. The fix is to compare against the value you expect (here, the email without the `+{cuid}` suffix), as the managed-user spec already does at lines 651 and 677.

::diff{file="apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/controllers/e2e/seated-bookings.e2e-spec.ts" lines="276-283"}

The same pattern appears at seated-bookings.e2e-spec.ts line 424 (`attendee?.displayEmail`) and team-bookings.e2e-spec.ts line 936 (`phoneBasedBooking.attendees[0].displayEmail`).
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/controllers/e2e/seated-bookings.e2e-spec.ts` (around lines 280 and 424) and `team-bookings.e2e-spec.ts` (around line 936), the `displayEmail` expectation reads its value from the response it checks (e.g. `createdSeatedBooking.attendees[0].displayEmail`). That makes the assertion pass even when the field is missing, because Jest's toEqual ignores undefined. Replace each with the literal expected value: the attendee's email with the `+{cuid}` suffix removed (or the original email when there is no suffix). Follow the explicit-value style used in `managed-user-bookings.e2e-spec.ts` around lines 651-681.

findings.title: Unused static helper duplicates the service's regex logic
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/outputs/booking.output.ts`, the `static cleanEmailForDisplay` method on `BookingAttendee` (around lines 59-62) is never called. `OutputBookingsService_2024_08_13.getDisplayEmail` in `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts` implements the same regex. Delete the unused static method. If you want a single source of truth, move the regex into a shared util and import it from both files.

findings.title: Unbound method reference passed to map
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`, `getOutputBooking` (around lines 166-173) passes the unbound `this.getDisplayEmail` to `.map`. Change it to `.map((guest: string) => this.getDisplayEmail(guest))` to match the arrow-function form used in the recurring-booking method a few lines below.

findings.title: OpenAPI JSON hand-edited with broken indentation
findings.fixPrompt: In `docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json`, four `"required": [` lines (around lines 31729, 31833, 32267, 33370) lost their indentation in a hand edit. Regenerate the OpenAPI spec with the project's generator (the one used for the 2024-08-13 booking DTOs) instead of editing it manually, so the output matches the generator's formatting.

findings.title: oasdiff errors suppressed wholesale without explanation
findings.fixPrompt: In `.github/oasdiff-err-ignore.txt`, six entries were added (lines 5-10) to suppress oasdiff errors for booking endpoint `oneOf` changes. Add a brief reason for each suppression (or a single comment at the top of the block) explaining why the change is non-breaking, and add a trailing newline at end of file. If a narrower pattern can match the intended change without hiding future breaks, use it.

findings.title: Seated attendee privacy deletion is preserved
findings.body: Seated-booking attendee `bookingFieldsResponses.email` is still removed in both seated paths (`delete attendeeParsed.bookingFieldsResponses.email`). `displayEmail` is only added at the attendee object level, next to `attendee.email`, which was already returned. The PR therefore does not expose any email that was previously hidden. The helper is not applied to seated `bookingFieldsResponses`, so the privacy deletion can't be undone by accident.

findings.title: Managed-user e2e tests assert exact stripped values
findings.body:
The new `displayEmail fields` block in `managed-user-bookings.e2e-spec.ts` checks the host, attendee, `bookingFieldsResponses`, and `displayGuests` paths against explicit values: `firstManagedUserEmail` and `secondManagedUserEmail` are fixed strings, so `toEqual` against them checks the stripped result directly. It also keeps the raw `email` assertions alongside, which verifies that backward compatibility holds.

::code{file="apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/controllers/e2e/managed-user-bookings.e2e-spec.ts" lines="648-682"}

findings.title: Reassignment output and host mapping covered for the empty-user case
findings.body: `getOutputReassignedBooking` and `getHost` both handle a missing user: `displayEmail` is `"unknown"` (or `getDisplayEmail("unknown")`), which matches the existing `"unknown"` placeholder for `email`. The reassignment test expectations for `displayEmail` match the non-suffixed team user emails.
